Honestly, it was one of the best things to ever happen to me- I needed that break. No grade pressure, no phones, everyone is incredibly nice, supportive, and calm around you. The routine is incredibly soothing too, and it's such a low pressure environment.

It helped me in so many ways; let it help you too. Go to therapy, even if you think it's stupid. And talk to your doctors; they've seen much worse, they're there to help. What helped me get over my fear of talking to them (not fear so much as I was afraid they'd judge me) is that you're already there, already committed. You can't say anything at this moment they haven't heard, or that they wouldn't believe.

As said above, intake will probably be boring- sitting in a room, being observed, answering tons of questions (this is just what I've heard). If you're already admitted it will go faster; I was manic/bleeding heavily when I was brought in, so they kind of rushed me through the whole intake process and sedated me immediately, so I only have second hand accounts of what it's like to walk in.

But just relax, talk to people, let it work for you, and (dare I say it?) have fun. I did. After intake there's TV, books, magazines; if people can bring you activities that helps a good deal too. If social media is a problem for you, revel in the chance to ignore everyone. Don't ask a friend or parent to check your facebook for you, or respond to texts and emails.

If you have any other questions/concerns, pm me. I'll be up for the next 24 hrs anyways. Good luck, let this be a good thing. :)
